### Donor Retention Benchmarks for Nonprofits (2025-2026)

Donor retention rates measure the percentage of last year's donors who give again this year (annual year-over-year, the most common metric). Sector averages vary by source, nonprofit size, donor segment, and measurement type, but typically range **35-55% overall**. Rates are higher for repeat donors and larger gifts, lower for new/micro donors. Top performers (e.g., top quartile) often exceed **65-70%**.

Key benchmarks from recent reports (primarily 2025-2026 data):

#### Overall Donor Retention Rates
| Source | Year | Overall Rate | Notes |
|--------|------|--------------|-------|
| Keela [1] | 2025 | 30-40% (average); 40-50% (above avg.); 50%+ (excellent) | Sector-wide; smaller orgs/missions like religious often higher. |
| Virtuous (771 mid-sized US nonprofits) [2] | 2026 | **54.73%** (avg.); **69.64%** (top quartile) | Highest benchmark; emphasizes relationship focus. |
| 4aGoodCause (FEP-based) [3] | 2025-2026 | **42.9%** | Overall avg. from Fundraising Effectiveness Project (FEP). |
| NextAfter (digital-first orgs) [4] | 2023 | **52.86%** (avg.); up to 86% | Digital channels boost retention across segments. |
| DonorSearch/Fundraising Report Card [5,7] | Recent | ~**35%** (avg.); **53.65%** (repeat) | Aim to hit 35% then improve; $0.20 cost per retained $ vs. acquisition. |
| CCS Fundraising [8] | 2025 | **46%** | Internal avg. for goal-setting. |
| Bloomerang/FEP Q3 [6] | 2025 | **31.9%** | Quarterly; up slightly from 2024; declining in major donor segments. |

#### By Donor Segment (FEP 2025 data, via Keela [1] & Bloomerang [6])
Higher retention for repeats/larger gifts; new donors are the biggest drop-off risk.
| Segment | Retention Rate | % of Donors | % of Revenue | Notes |
|---------|----------------|-------------|--------------|-------|
| **New Donors** | 14.0-19.4% | - | - | First-to-second gift: **25.84%** avg., **37.86%** top quartile [2]; ~3/4 never return. |
| **Repeat Donors** | **43.6-69.2%** | - | 61.6% | Most stable; up 0.2 pp in 2025 [1,3,6]. Recurring monthly: up to 90% [3]. |
| Micro ($1-100) | **21.3%** | 50.9% | 1.6% | Lowest retention. |
| Small ($101-500) | **37.5%** | 29.5% | 11.5% | - |
| Midsize ($501-5K) | **48.8%** | 17.2% | 30.6% | - |
| Major ($5K-50K) | **52.0%** | 2.0% | 25.2% | Down 1 pp YoY [6]. |
| Supersize ($50K+) | **56.6%** | 0.4% | 52.3% | Highest [1,6]. |

#### By Gift Frequency (FEP 2025, via Bloomerang [6])
More gifts = higher retention:
- 1-time: **19.2%**
- 2-time: **38.5%**
- 3-6 times: **62.5%**
- 7+ times: **87.3%**

#### Other Metrics [2]
- **Gift Frequency**: 4.15 gifts/donor/year (avg.); 6.62 (top quartile).

#### Realistic Goals
- **Small nonprofits (<1,000 donors)**: 35-45% [3].
- Focus on **second gift** (key retention signal) and **monthly giving** for sustainability.
- Track via: Annual (YoY), cohort (by acquisition year), rolling (last 12 months), or campaign-specific.

**Why it matters**: Retaining donors costs ~1/5th of acquisition [5]; repeats drive 60%+ revenue [1]. Benchmarks dipped slightly in new donors (18.1% Q1 2025 [9]), but digital/relationship strategies lift rates [4]. For latest FEP, check quarterly updates. Sources: Linked in search results [1-10].
